questions.question: For how many years does the Indian Vice - President hold office?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Vice-President holds office for a term of five years.**
 
• The Vice-President is **elected indirectly by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.**
 
• The Vice-President can be removed from office by a resolution passed by the** Rajya Sabha by an absolute majority.**
 
• The Vice-President can preside over the **Rajya Sabha and perform other functions as assigned by the President of India.**
 
• ** Option 1 is the correct answer as the Vice-President of India holds office for a term of five years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term of a member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian Parliament, is six years.
 
• The term of a member of the Lok Sabha, the lower house of the Indian Parliament, is five years.

questions.question: Which among the following was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan?

• **The correct answer is Aurangzeb. He was the sixth Mughal emperor and ruled from 1658 to 1707.**

 
 
• Aurangzeb was born on October 24, 1618, as the third son of Shahjahan and Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He was given the title of "Alamgir" which means "Conqueror of the World".
 
 
 
• **Jahangir was the fourth Mughal emperor **and ruled from 1605 to 1627. He was the son of Akbar and the father of Shahjahan.
 
• **Humayun was the second Mughal emperor **and ruled from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.
 
 
• He was the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal dynasty.
 
 
 
• Sikander Lodhi was the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate from 1489 to 1517.
 
 
• He was not a Mughal emperor.
 
 
 
• **Hence, the statement "Aurangzeb was the son of the Mughal emperor Shahjahan" is correct.**

questions.question: Who among the following was a Shaka ruler in India (AD 130 - 150)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudradaman.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3, Rudradaman.** 
 
• ** The Shaka rulers** were a group of nomadic people who migrated from Central Asia to various parts of India from the **2nd century BCE to the 4th century CE.**
 
• **Rudradaman was a Shaka ruler** who ruled over the western Indian region of Malwa and** parts of Gujarat from around AD 130 to 150.**
 
• He was known for his military campaigns against other regional powers like th**e Satavahanas and the Yaudheyas.**
 
• ** Rudradaman is also famous for his rock inscriptions**, particularly the Junagadh inscription in Gujarat, which gives us valuable information about his reign and the political situation of his time.
 
• The other options in the question are also related to Indian history but are not Shaka rulers.
 
• **Bindusara was a Mauryan emperor who ruled in the 3rd century BCE,** Panduka was a Kushan king who ruled in the 1st century CE, and Chashtana was a Parthian king who ruled in the 2nd century CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Shaka rulers were also known as the Scythians in ancient literature**.

 
 
• They were mainly concentrated in western and central India, and their reigns overlapped with those of other regional powers like the Satavahanas, the Kushans, and the Guptas.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara was the son of the famous Mauryan emperor Chandragupta Maurya and ruled over a vast empire that included much of modern-day India**.
 
 
• He was known for his diplomatic skills and his patronage of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Panduka was a Kushan king who ruled parts of northern India, Central Asia, and China.**
 
 
• He was a patron of Buddhism, and his reign saw the spread of Gandhara art, which combined Indian and Greek artistic styles.
 
 
 
• **Chashtana** also known as Caṣṭana, was a prominent ruler of the Saka Western Satraps in northwestern India during the 1st and 2nd centuries CE. His reign, spanning from approximately 78 to 130 CE, marked a significant period of expansion and stability for the dynasty.

__
 
• **As per the new regime Income Tax Slab Rates FY 2021 - 22, the tax slab applicable for Sam, who has an income of 9 lakh rupees yearly, is 0.15.**

• The new regime Income Tax Slab Rates **FY 2021 - 22 was announced in the Union Budget 2021 by the Finance Minister.**
 
• The new regime offers lower tax rates without deductions or exemptions.
 
• The tax slab rate for an individual having an annual income of **up to Rs. 2.5 lakh is 0%.**
 
• For an individual having an annual income between **Rs. 2.5 lakh to Rs. 5 lacks, the tax slab rate is 5%.**
 
• For an individual having an annual income between **Rs. 5 lahks to Rs. 7.5 lakh, the tax slab rate is 10%**.
 
• For an individual having an annual income between** Rs. 7.5 lakh to Rs. 10 lahks, the tax slab rate is 15%.**
 
• The tax slab rates go up to 30% for individuals having an annual income above Rs. 15 lahks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution talks about a uniform civil code?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• **Article 44 talks about a uniform civil code in India.**
 
• A uniform civil code is a proposal to replace personal laws based on religion with a common set of laws for all citizens irrespective of their religion.
 
• This would ensure gender equality and social justice.
 
• 'Uniform Civil Code' is explicitly mentioned in Part 4, Article 44 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• Article 44 says, “The State shall endeavor to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.
 
• ”Uniform Civil Code is a proposal in India to formulate and implement secular personal laws of citizens which apply on all citizens equally regardless of their religion.
 
• Currently, the personal laws of various communities are governed by their religious scriptures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 352 **is related to the proclamation of emergency, while Article 14 talks about equality before the law and equal protection of laws for all citizens.
 
• **Article 370 **is related to the special status of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The debate over a uniform civil code is ongoing, and it remains to be seen whether it will be implemented in the future.

questions.question: ______ is the division of the cytoplasm of one eukaryotic cell into two daughter cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Cytokinesis.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The correct option is "Cytokinesis".**
 
• **Cytokinesis is the process by which the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell divides into two daughter cells after mitosis or meiosis.**
 
• During cytokinesis, a contractile ring made of actin and myosin filaments forms around the cell, which then contracts and divides the cytoplasm into two parts.
 
• ** In animal cells, cytokinesis** results in the formation of a cleavage furrow, while in plant cells, a cell plate forms in the middle of the cell and grows outward until it reaches the cell wall.
 
• **Cytokinesis is a crucial step in cell division,** as it ensures that each daughter cell receives a complete set of chromosomes and other cellular components necessary for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition caused by the body's response to an infection**. It has no relation to cytokinesis.
 
• **Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus of a eukaryotic **cell into two daughter nuclei during cell division. It is different from cytokinesis, which involves the division of the cytoplasm.
 
• **Genesis refers to the beginning or origin** of something and has no relation to cell division or cytokinesis.

questions.question: Which Indian state is home to the Buddhist cave temples known as Barabar Caves?

__
 
• **The correct answer is Bihar.**
 
• **The Barabar Caves are a group of rock-cut caves located in the Makhdumpur region of Jehanabad district in Bihar.**
 
• These caves are considered to be some of the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India and date back to the** Mauryan period (322-185 BCE).**
 
• The caves were initially used by** Ajivikas, a sect of ascetics, before being taken over by Buddhists.**
 
• The caves are known for their unique architecture and intricate carvings, with some of the caves having a polished and highly finished surface.

questions.question: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** stratification.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stratification refers to the arrangement of different species in an ecosystem based on their vertical distribution.**
 
• **This vertical distribution is determined by factors such as light availability, temperature, and moisture levels.**
 
• Different species occupy different levels in the ecosystem, with some living closer to the ground or water surface, while others live higher up in the canopy or upper water layers.
 
• Stratification is important for the functioning of an ecosystem, as it allows for the coexistence of different species with different resource requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biomagnification **refers to the process by which certain substances, such as toxins or pollutants, become more concentrated as they move up the food chain. 
 
• **Coevolution** refers to the reciprocal evolutionary changes that occur between two or more species that interact with each other.
 
• **Decomposition** refers to the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms, which releases nutrients back into the ecosystem
